name: collapsible-column
title: Collapsible weather column
summary: A narrow weather widget at four heights: a collapsibleColumn keeps city and temperature (no priority), then the icon, high/low and condition by vertical collapsiblePriority, and three tied forecast rows that drop from the bottom up.
prompt: A tall, narrow weather widget (city, sun icon, temperature, condition, high/low, three hourly forecast rows) that sheds content as it gets shorter: the forecast rows go first from the bottom, then the condition, then high/low, then the icon; city and temperature always stay. Show it at 256, 208, 164 and 100 dp.
teaches: Stack a widget's content in a collapsibleColumn so rows that don't fit the height are dropped instead of clipped
Rank the rows with collapsiblePriority {orientation: vertical, priority: N}; leave the rows that must stay (city, temperature) without one
Give repeated rows the same priority: tied children keep document order, so the forecast drops from the bottom row up
Put the padding and background on a wrapping box and give the collapsibleColumn fillMaxSize, so fillMaxWidth rows stay inside the padding
pitfalls: The priority's orientation must match the container: a horizontal collapsiblePriority on a collapsibleColumn child is ignored and the child counts as unprioritized (kept first)

A collapsibleColumn's own padding is not applied to its children's fill width: a fillMaxWidth row inside a padded collapsibleColumn comes out as wide as the column and offset by -padding (Java, matched by both players). Pad a wrapping box instead
Rows are kept in priority order, not document order: at 164 dp high/low (priority 3) stays while the condition above it (priority 2) goes, and the remaining rows close up

Dropping stops at the first row that does not fit: every row after it in priority order goes too, even one small enough for the space left (a 10 dp priority-1 row is dropped under a 40 dp priority-2 row that did not fit). Give similar-sized rows adjacent priorities
Give the rows fixed heights (here 20–48 dp boxes) when the result has to be predictable: a text's height depends on the font and the player

A row of fixed-width demo cards is wider than a narrow host: give the row a horizontalScroll (bound to a variable — a literal position leaves its touch expression unused, which the audit reports as dead code)

snippets.note: the collapsibleColumn with its eight rows, inside the padded card box
condition, vertical priority 2: goes before high/low (3) and the icon (4)
a forecast row, priority 1: the three tie and drop bottom-up

check.describe: Four cards: the first fills the height (256 dp at 300) and shows everything; 208 dp keeps one forecast row; 164 dp keeps city, icon, temperature and high/low (the condition and forecast are gone); 100 dp keeps city and temperature only. Verified against Java (java-layout.sh 360 300): the same rows are gone and the C++ and TS bounds match it. Resized: the full-height card is the live one — at 360×200 it (and the taller fixed cards, squeezed to the row) keep city, icon and temperature; at 360×400 it shows everything with room to spare; at 240 wide the row scrolls horizontally (horizontalScroll) rather than cutting the last card.
